First off, you need a food storage. There's no if, ands, or buts about it. If you're able, stockpile food. This isn't just a WWIII or Civil War scenario. You suddenly find your money is very tight or there was a natural disaster. There's a million scenarios where a food storage would be useful.

Dried foods

  • Dried beans, rice, pasta, oats, grains, instant potatoes, boxed meals, etc.
  • Cheap, especially in bulk
  • Store in factory airtight bags to prevent moisture, bugs, and other stuff
  • Downside - Usually requires water

Canned Foods

  • Beans, veggies, fruit, potatoes, spam, vienna sausage, tuna, soups, tomato sauce, etc
  • You don't have to worry about storage conditions as much as dried food
  • Require no preparation. Can be eaten cold from the can
  • Vienna sausage and spam are high in calories. They're the only meat you can store without refrigeration.
  • Jerky doesn't count. It's too expensive for a bulk food storage. You're stuck with spam.
  • A spare can opener might come in handy
  • Do Not Waste The Juice. Drink It!

Other Food Stuff

  • Comfort Foods- Jerky, chips, hot chocolate, (hard) candy, pudding, water flavor, coffee, tea
  • Honey- This can replace jelly and syrup. Last forever, although it might crystallize. This is fine and fairly common.
  • Vinegar- If you like it, it's good to have. No point if you hate it though.
  • Sugar- Make sure you store it properly
  • Salt, Pepper, Spices, Seasonings- You know what these are for.
  • Backpacking meals- expensive, but great for the lazy people.
  • Survival meals (Military MREs)- Complete meals and high in calories. These are great for emergency evacuation.

WATER!

  • 1 gallon of Drinking water per day (about 4 liters)
  • Use this for drinking/consumption only
  • Store more if you have more dried than canned foods
  • Store much more if you live in dry areas (like Arizona)
  • Good luck storing 400 Gallons. Get a Water Filter.
  • Here's a common type for backpackers. Example 1 and 2
  • Make sure you have enough filters. The above are rated up to 300 and 500 Gallons respectively
  • Bleach, Purification Tablets, and Boiling can also purify water. This doesn't remove the particles though.

How much food should i store?
If your budget is very tight,1-2 week minimum. This will be about $50 or less. If you can afford it, store at 3 months minimum. This is where buying in bulk and shopping around for the best prices come in handy. Many recommend up to a year, but this would require constantly cycling thorough your perishables and slowly building up your storage.

How much water should i store?
You should have at minimum a 2 week supply. However, you should store as much water as you feel comfortable with. This should be about 1 gal per day or 2 cases per week. A case of water is 3.16 gallons (16.9 ounces x 24 bottles). Buy the cheapest ones you can find. You should be able to find them for $3 or less per case. Buying the gallon jugs should cost you no more than $1/gal. I'd recommend at least a few of the gallon jugs if you have a water filter. Store more if you live in a dry environment.
